info.name: url-crawler
info.description: The url-crawler job service. Start it with `docker compose up --build -d`, then run Submit a crawl first: it stores the new id in the crawlId variable that every other request uses. Every tunable value is a collection variable, so edit the seed, the page cap, the concurrency, the batch size and the cursor in the Variables tab rather than in the requests. Every saved example below is a real response, captured against https://crawler-test.com.

request.description:
200 once the API has run a SELECT 1 against Postgres. 503 when the database is unreachable.

---

### Example responses, captured from a live run

**200 OK**

```json
{
  "status": "ok"
}
```

**503 database unavailable**

```json
{
  "detail": "database unavailable"
}
```

request.description:
Queues a crawl and returns 202 with a Location header. The crawl runs on a worker, not in the API. Edit seed, maxPages and concurrency in the Variables tab; the two numbers are unquoted in the body because the API rejects them as strings. The test script stores the new id in crawlId, so every request below works with no copying.

---

### Example responses, captured from a live run

**202 Accepted**

```json
{
  "id": "47833935-0ac8-4abc-b8c7-bc31e4849bd5",
  "seed": "https://crawler-test.com/",
  "state": "queued",
  "config": {
    "timeout": 10.0,
    "max_bytes": 5000000,
    "max_pages": 25,
    "concurrency": 5,
    "respect_robots": true
  },
  "created_at": "2026-09-12T17:41:11.480048Z",
  "started_at": null,
  "finished_at": null,
  "attempts": 0,
  "cancel_requested": false,
  "stats": null,
  "error": null
}
```

request.description:
One object per page fetched, readable while the crawl is still running. pageLimit sets the batch size. Keyset pagination: next_after is null once you have read everything written so far, which is not the same as the crawl being over. The test script copies next_after into afterSeq for the request below.

---

### Example responses, captured from a live run

**200 first batch**

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "seq": 1,
      "url": "https://crawler-test.com/",
      "status": 200,
      "error": null,
      "links": [
        "https://crawler-test.com/",
        "https://crawler-test.com/mobile/separate_desktop",
        "https://crawler-test.com/mobile/desktop_with_AMP_as_mobile",
        "https://crawler-test.com/mobile/separate_desktop_with_different_h1",
        "... 407 more"
      ],
      "fetched_at": "2026-09-12T17:41:12.571882Z"
    },
    {
      "seq": 2,
      "url": "https://crawler-test.com/mobile/separate_desktop",
      "status": 200,
      "error": null,
      "links": [
        "https://crawler-test.com/"
      ],
      "fetched_at": "2026-09-12T17:41:12.695055Z"
    },
    {
      "seq": 3,
      "url": "https://crawler-test.com/mobile/separate_desktop_with_different_links_in",
      "status": 200,
      "error": null,
      "links": [
        "https://crawler-test.com/"
      ],
      "fetched_at": "2026-09-12T17:41:12.807897Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_after": 3
}
```

request.description:
A request, not a kill. A queued crawl aborts outright. A running one stops at its worker's next heartbeat and keeps the pages it already wrote. A finished one is returned unchanged.

---

### Example responses, captured from a live run

**202 aborted**

```json
{
  "id": "f2b70430-e364-4f14-86cb-f919d0ebfdef",
  "state": "aborted"
}
```

A request, not a kill. A queued crawl aborts outright. A running one stops at its worker's next heartbeat and keeps the pages it already wrote. A finished one is returned unchanged.

```json

  "id": "f2b70430-e364-4f14-86cb-f919d0ebfdef",
  "state": "aborted"
}
```

variable.description: The crawl every request below reads. Submit a crawl fills this in from its 202 response, so you never copy an id by hand.
Page cap for the submitted crawl. Unquoted in the body: the API wants a number.
Worker tasks inside the crawl, 1 to 50. Unquoted in the body: the API wants a number.
Page batch size for the pages endpoint, 1 to 500.
Keyset cursor for the pages endpoint: the seq to read after. Read the pages copies its next_after here, so Read the next batch continues where it stopped.
A seed on a link-local address, to demonstrate the refused-seed 422.
